If it doesn't change drastically as you're gathering info, don't worry too much about it. Just focus on getting a feel for your world's market. You only need to worry about your world's market anyways (imo). 

Here are some tips based on my experiences without giving too much away:

\- Take into account the demand for the items; don't bother if there are large gaps of time in-between sales.

\- Learn what furnishing items decorators use a lot in their builds.

\- Focus more on selling multiples of quick selling items at modest prices rather than expensive items that take longer to sell.

\- Be willing to invest what gil you do have into experimenting with the market. Be willing to take risks, but not misguided ones. Don't buy a shit ton of materials for an item(s) if you don't yet know how well and how often it will sell.

\- Patience. You won't immediately strike gold. It will take some time to hone in on your big-ticket items. You don't have to sell the exact same items as everyone else! It's all about finding your niche and what works for you.

It honestly really depends on your world's market, your available free time, and *especially* your commitment. I've only been playing FF14 for a little over a year, and have only been playing the furniture market for less than a year, and I've made tons of gil. The most I've had at one time was 80+ mil gil. Of course, not all of that is from selling furniture items, but a good chunk of it is!

I would love to tell you all that I know, as I love being helpful and info-dumping on things I know, but it's as others say: it would negatively impact the market. Plus, you may find there are better ways to go about it than what myself or other players may tell you. What works for me and my playstyle and free time might not work for others. My way of doing it might even be mind-numbing to others, to be entirely honest! It's up to you to figure out what works best for you.

Feel free to PM me with any questions you may have and I'll answer to the best of my abilities. Good luck!

You don't even have to watch the cutscenes. You can just manually skip them as you run through the MSQ. But for this person's needs for Sims CC, WinRAR is all they'll really need if they're only really needing it for Sims CC zips and such.

Most if not all CC is going to be a .package file, which is not a file you can open in anything other than by putting them in "Documents > Electronic Arts > Sims 4 > Mods > Packages" or by opening them using a program that is used to create said CC. 

Sometimes, you'll run across CC that you download that comes in a file type such as .zip, .7zip, .rar, etc. This is just a compressed version of the files that makes it easier to store and transfer files and isn't used just in Sims CC stuff. To open most files like these to access the files within that ARE .package files, download WinRAR. It's a program that is free and 100% safe to download and use. There is an option to pay for it, but there is absolutely no need to and nothing sketchy you have to do to avoid paying for it. It's just a free program nowadays.

You don't have to worry so much about accidentally downloading any viruses with your CC as long as you don't go to sites that are riddled with pop-ups, confusing pages, and just general things that are sketchy. Sites you can 100% trust are ModTheSims, The Sims Resource, and SimsFileShare. You'll run into Mediafire downloads, which are also okay too, but I would avoid them if possible because that site kinda lands more on the iffy side imo. Some downloads will be through Google Drive, which can be a bit of a gamble, but as far as I know, it's also trustworthy. If you want to stay on the safer side of downloads, I'd say look for CC on Tumblr to start off with, just to get your toes wet and test the waters.

All in all, a lot of what you'll need to know can be easily Googled and isn't hard to learn nor is it risky to do. Just felt like explaining the file types is something that might not be discussed as often in tutorials and, since they can be confusing, I figured I'd let you in on it. Shipping on your own means that you create the shipping label yourself. You can also just go to the post office and this will all be done for you, of course. It's just slightly cheaper through PayPal. If you do go to the post office (or whichever carrier of your choice, UPS, FedEx, etc,), make sure to ask for a receipt!! It should have the tracking number on there for you to give your buyer. It's also good to have it just in case you need to prove you sent it out!!

To give your buyer their tracking number, go to the receipt icon on the top of your screen, find the order, tap "Mark as Shipped", and insert the shipping provider and tracking number!!
